title: Signal Weaving — Weekly Commitment Ledger (Personal KPI Draft)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a lightweight, lo-fi ledger for tracking one-person KPI experiments and weekly commitments. The metaphor is "signal weaving": small, intentional threads (habits, micro-projects, experiments) woven together to produce a visible outcome signal at the end of each sprint (2 weeks).

Goals for this doc:
- Capture weekly commitments in a way that prioritizes attention budget and energy, not just task count.
- Track 2 leading signals and 1 lagging outcome per micro-OKR.
- Keep entries short, timestamped, and actionable so the ledger stays scannable.

How I use this (process):
1) Preflight (5 minutes, Monday morning) — quick check before starting the week: energy, calendar density, one big focus item.
2) Commit (10 minutes) — write 2 micro-OKRs for the week. Each has: intent, leading signal, lagging outcome, timebox.
3) Midweek pulse (Wednesday, 10 minutes) — short note: friction, what to drop, what to double down.
4) Retro (Friday afternoon, 20 minutes) — fill the retro prompts below and adjust next week's commitments.

Weekly template (exactly what I fill):
- Week: 2025-03-03 → 2025-03-09
- Energy score (0–10): 6 (notes: sleep ok, travel on Thu)
- Calendar load: heavy (6 meetings/day Tue–Thu)

Micro-OKR A (Growth of writing habit):
- Intent: Ship 3 short notes (300–500 words) that explore inference optimization stories for internal knowledge share.
- Leading signals (choose 2): write-streak (days with >=30 mins), headline-sent (number of headlines drafted), first-paragraph-started.
- Lagging outcome: 3 notes published to team drive + 1 internal share post.
- Timebox: 2 x 45-minute writing blocks on Mon & Thu mornings.
- Confidence: 0.7
- Risk: calendar interruptions, over-editing.
- Quick plan: use 5-minute preflight, timer set, accept one rough draft per note.

Micro-OKR B (Quality signal for prompt evaluation harness):
- Intent: run 50 paired prompt samples across two model variants, track regressions.
- Leading signals: samples processed (count), evaluation-run-completed (boolean).
- Lagging outcome: concise summary with 3 candidate changes to prompt templates.
- Timebox: 3 × 30 min test runs Tue/Wed/Fri morning.
- Confidence: 0.6
- Risk: infra flakiness, dataset edge cases.
- Quick plan: limit to a single dataset slice, log failures to a shared spreadsheet (link to be added).

Measurement rules (how I score signals):
- Leading signals are binary or small integers (easy to update).
- Lagging outcomes must be measurable (publish, PR merged, dashboard updated).
- Add a decay multiplier to multi-week signals: if a signal hasn't been touched in 2 weeks, reduce weight by 0.5.

Midweek pulse example (Wed 2025-03-05):
- A: writing: 1 block completed (draft 1/3). Good momentum but edits creeping. Action: lock edits for 24h.
- B: eval harness: infra intermittent; only 20/50 samples processed. Action: escalate to infra-sre thread, pivot to local sampling for remainder.

Retro prompts (Friday):
- What shipped? (be specific)
- What signal moved the most? (leading/lagging)
- What was the friction point? Where did energy leak?
- What did I drop that I should have kept? What did I keep that I should have dropped?
- One change for next week (small, reversible).
- Quick gratitude note (1 sentence).

Retro entry (Fri 2025-03-07):
- Shipped: 1 draft note published (A: 1/3), internal TODO doc for eval harness with 20 samples processed.
- Signal moved: write-streak stayed alive but headline-sent count low (1 draft headline).
- Friction: meeting overload on Thu killed the second writing block; infra flakiness slowed evals.
- Drop/Keep: Dropped thorough editing (good drop). Kept detailed logging for evals (good keep).
- Change for next week: move writing blocks earlier (first thing) and reduce meeting hours on Tue by blocking focus time.
- Gratitude: had a really clear 30-minute walk that helped the writing rhythm.

Open experiments and hypotheses (ongoing):
- Hypothesis 1: Time-of-day batching (write at 08:00) increases draft throughput by 2x vs evening. Experiment: 2-week A/B on start time.
- Hypothesis 2: Reducing meeting tempo on heavy days yields at least one additional 45-min focus window, which correlates with a +1 writing draft per week.
- Hypothesis 3: Using a short evaluation rubric (3 bullets) reduces over-editing time by 30%.

Failure modes (notes to self):
- Over-indexing on output count (ship thin content). Mitigation: require 1 qualitative note per draft explaining tradeoffs.
- Context switching due to infra tickets. Mitigation: reserve a 60-min "ticket triage" block separate from focus blocks.
- Losing signal faith: if a leading signal drops twice, pause the experiment and re-evaluate.

Mini-checklist for Monday preflight:
- [ ] Energy score logged
- [ ] Two micro-OKRs written
- [ ] Meetings triaged: block 2 focus windows
- [ ] Timer set for first block

Notes, random observations (scratchpad):
- Noticed my best writing when physical pen used for headline sketches (small cognitive change). Try a pen-headline step for 2 weeks.
- The phrase "signal weaving" is useful when describing tradeoffs to teammates; keeps conversation about attention, not vanity metrics.
- Consider a monthly "signal audit": which micro-OKRs produced long-term value vs noise?

Backlog (things I might commit next week):
- Build a tiny spreadsheet to track leading signal trendlines (simple sparklines).
- Draft a 1-pager on prompt-eval sampling heuristics for the team.
- Try a 3-day focus sprint (no meetings) to test high-intensity writing.

Sidenote on metrics I refuse to chase (mental model):
- I will not optimize for raw token count or hours logged. I want signal density: what measurable change happened because I spent the time.

End-of-doc: small accountability ask: once a month I will ping Maya or Liam with the month's top 2 outcomes and one ask (help, review, or shove a blocker).

-- end ledger entry --
